jamie: FYI — after the kernel fusion merge yesterday I'm seeing a p99 regression on model-x (stable workload). p95 up a bit, but p99 tail jumps ~60ms compared to baseline. Dumped a profiler and KV traces to s3://redwood-perf/model-x/2480001111/profile.tar.gz :eyes:
sasha: ugh. can you paste the flame or top stacks? any correlation with sequence length or kv-miss rate?
alex: quick summary from the trace: two hot paths — (1) fused-cuda-kernel init stalls when an incoming request triggers a kernel variant switch, (2) KV cache miss spikes for requests with tail token lengths > 1200. combined effect: some microbatches get delayed while we cold-init fallback kernels + rehydrate KV.
alex: repro profiling snippet (ran on a canary GPU):
```
./bin/prof --model model-x --trace kv,kernel-switch,dispatch --window 120s --out /tmp/mx.prof
# output: top stacks show kernel_loader::select_variant -> cuda_module::load -> wait_on_mutex
```
jamie: important datapoints: avg_seq_len=420, p95=42ms, p99=108ms (after deploy). Before merge p99 was 48ms. kv cache hitrate for route-prod was 92% -> dropped to 78% for sequences >1k.
marta: hypothesis: fusion introduces extra variant churn for mixed-length traffic. when a long request arrives it forces a path that invalidates the small-seq kernel's KV mapping, causing a cascade of cold paths and stalled microbatches.
sasha: can we mitigate by tweaking scheduler params? proposed quick experiments: 1) decrease max_batch_tokens for mixed routes so fewer long requests join short microbatches, 2) lower max_wait_ms to reduce tail coalescing, 3) route long-seq requests to dedicated non-fused kernel pool.
jamie: config we tried locally that helped p99 without huge throughput loss:
```json
{"max_batch_tokens": "4096", "max_wait_ms": "10", "microbatch_prefer_short": "true"}
```
results: p95 ~40ms, p99 ~72ms, throughput -6% on this canary.
alex: another quick patch that reduced kernel load churn: add a small sequence-length bucketing before batch join. pseudo: `if seq_len > 1024: queue_long.push(req) else: queue_short.push(req)` then select kernels per queue. simple but reduces cross-variant joins.
marta: also saw that KV rehydrate latency is dominated by a mutex in the cache loader (kv_store::rehydrate). lock contention increases when many long-seq misses happen concurrently. worth profiling lock hotpath.
sasha: alternative: relax kernel selector to prefer compatibility over micro-optimizations when current queue has mix of seq lengths. i.e., if mix_ratio > 0.2 choose generic kernel that avoids variant init. tradeoff expected: small p95 penalty but big p99 reduction.
ajex: (typo) alex: i ran a 2-hour experiment comparing strategies: bucketed queues + max_wait_ms=12 => p99 68ms, throughput -4%. selector-relax => p99 64ms, throughput -9%. per-model routing to non-fused => p99 58ms, throughput -11% but much more stable tail.
jamie: sounds like per-route policy is the winner for tail-critical routes. for PLG routes we prefer higher throughput and accept bigger tail. need automated policy that picks per-route SLO (p95 target, p99 budget) and sets scheduler knobs accordingly.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: runtime/2026-03-17T21:10 utc (canary) -> policies/route-model-x/experiment-2480001111
sasha: next steps: 1) add lock profiler for KV rehydrate (low overhead), 2) run 48h canary of per-route non-fused pool and collect p50/p95/p99 + cost delta, 3) implement bucketed queue prototype with low-risk rollout flag.
marta: I'll open a PR with the bucketed queue and a small adaptive max_wait_ms heuristic:
```
if avg_seq_len > 1024:
  max_batch_tokens = 8192
  max_wait_ms = 8
else:
  max_batch_tokens = 4096
  max_wait_ms = 18
```
we'll tune thresholds after the canary.
jamie: i will chart the canary in grafana (route-level heatmaps + kernel-switch events) and add remediation steps to the runtime runbook. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
alex: +1, also adding a perf regression test to CI that simulates mixed short+long traffic to catch similar regressions earlier.
jamie: thanks all — filing follow-ups: #1 bucketed-queue PR, #2 KV lock profiler, #3 canary policy + grafana dashboard. keeping this thread for notes.
